headline: Hackers stole significant data from Craneware, a tech firm used by thousands of US hospitals
summary: UK-based healthcare billing software maker Craneware confirmed a cyberattack led to the exfiltration of a "significant volume" of customer, employee, and partner data.
details: U.K.-based healthcare billing software maker Craneware is responding to a cyberattack where hackers stole a "significant volume" of customer data from its systems, the company announced.

The company stated that the hackers appear to have been expelled from its systems, but an investigation into the breach is ongoing. Craneware's flagship accounting and billing software is used by thousands of clinics, hospitals, and pharmacies across the United States.

While the exact types of data taken were not specified, Craneware confirmed a "percentage" of employee data, customer data, and partner records were exfiltrated. The company handles large amounts of medical records and patient data for its clients.
In 2021, Craneware acquired Florida-based pharmacy software maker Sentry, gaining access to 147 million patient records collected over two decades. It is unclear if these records were affected.

Craneware CEO Keith Neilson has not yet responded to inquiries regarding the incident, including whether the hackers made any demands like ransom, or if the company's systems can currently receive email.

This incident is the latest in a series of data breaches targeting tech companies that supply services to the U.S. healthcare sector. Compromising such software can grant hackers access to vast amounts of sensitive patient data.

Other recent breaches include TriZetto, which confirmed 3.4 million people's data stolen, CareCloud's breach of electronic health records, and Episource, which notified 5.4 million people of stolen information.
The largest U.S. medical data breach occurred in 2024 when Change Healthcare, owned by UnitedHealth, was hacked by a Russian ransomware gang. This incident affected at least 192 million people.

headline_marked: [[Claude 3.5 Sonnet is the New Default Workhorse]] for AI development
headline: Claude 3.5 Sonnet is the New Default Workhorse for AI development
summary: Anthropic's new model outperforms Claude 3 Opus in intelligence, operates at twice the speed, and costs significantly less, making it ideal for complex agentic systems.
details: Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet redefines the cost-performance curve for building AI products. It delivers intelligence superior to the previous top-tier Claude 3 Opus, while running at twice the speed and a substantially lower cost.
Positioned as the first in Anthropic's new 3.5 family, this mid-tier model surpasses Claude 3 Opus on graduate-level reasoning (GPQA) and coding proficiency (HumanEval) benchmarks.

The model is now available through the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud's Vertex AI. Its pricing is set at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, featuring a 200K token context window.

This combination of higher intelligence, reduced latency, and lower cost makes Claude 3.5 Sonnet ideal for high-throughput applications like context-sensitive customer support and orchestrating multi-step workflows.
For agentic workflows, Claude 3.5 Sonnet significantly improves performance, solving 64% of bug-fixing problems in internal evaluations, compared to Claude 3 Opus's 38% in the same tests.

Its sophisticated reasoning and troubleshooting capabilities allow it to independently write, edit, and execute code when provided with the right tools, making previously expensive or slow multi-model workflows viable.
Alongside the model, Anthropic introduced "Artifacts" on Claude.ai, a new feature that displays generated content like code snippets or website designs in a dedicated window next to the conversation.

This creates a dynamic workspace where users can see, edit, and build on Claude's output in real time. It supports generating and previewing HTML pages, SVG graphics, and interactive React components, streamlining the development process.
